newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors to seek arrest of bankers-radio.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors to seek arrest of bankers-radio.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors will seek arrest warrants for the heads of two leading local banks in connection with loans to insolvent Hanbo Steel Co, state radio said on Wednesday.
It said the two, Sheen Kwang-shik of Korea First Bank and Woo Chan-mok of Cho Hung Bank, would be charged with bribery. A prosecution spokesman said he could not confirm the radio report.
"The prosecution plans to seek arrest warrants for the two persons within today," Korea Broadcasting System said.
Prosecution officials said on Tuesday the bankers would be questioned on whether they received commissions in return for offering huge loans to Hanbo Steel, the country's second largest steelmaker.

Hanbo Steel, flagship of the Hanbo Group, the 14th largest conglomerate in South Korea, had piled up about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions before it was declared insolvent on January 23.
Prosecutors last Friday arrested Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo on charges of fraud and violating laws on cheques and trust and savings companies.
